chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from al-Qasim ibn Burayd from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who set up a net in the water, then returned to his house and left it standing, and later came to it and found fish in it that had died, he said: 'What his hand did [caused the death], so there is no objection to eating what fell into it.'
ai.seo_question: Is fish caught in a static net considered halal if it dies in the trap?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that fish caught in a static net are permissible (halal) because their death is attributed to the owner's initial act of setting the trap, rather than requiring ritual slaughter (dhikr) at the moment of death. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between animals killed by human agency versus those dying by natural causes or other means, affirming the permissibility of such catch without reciting Bismillah during the kill. The narration underscores the principle that the 'hand's work' (the setup) suffices for permissibility in the case of fish in water.
